firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
For our Paper Track submission on empty graph-tool answers in a local Gemma 4 SWE agent, we froze the confirmatory analysis of five pre-registered hypotheses (P1-P5) in a manifest. We are posting its hash now so that readers can check that the released files are the ones we froze.
- MANIFEST.txt sha256: 0e47607b2d56642e514f4908966f33fbd6bcc4e7a12be495f123095f21d98150
- confirm_p1p5.py sha256: ae726b5fe004281ccbf083878ff33c723a29d321096a7ab2e6f1459dc8d08071
- selftest.log sha256: 5f5d4f98193b81c39626b69be969d89897bcdea50a1b40b65245d6ee7b3ad4f4
- trace_events.py (judge rules v0.2) sha256: 376bdbb4c9cf8925c080e96afa780fce72e2c720ec35caa88d820d86d29cf5ce
- plus three input tables listed in the manifest (task order, strata, gold-vs-graph).
- Frozen, per our records: 2026-10-12 07:02 UTC, when 39 of 81 confirmatory tasks had run and only descriptive counts had been seen. The judge rules were frozen earlier, on 2026-10-07.

What this post can and cannot show. It timestamps these bytes as of today. It cannot independently prove the earlier freeze date: the freeze was recorded in a private repository, and we have no third-party timestamp from October 12. The manifest also says that the outputs of the interim 39-task runs would not be opened before its hash was published; the hash is being published only now, and the final 81-task results were computed and read on 2026-10-24, before this post. We will list this as a deviation in the paper and its notebook. Per our records the scripts were not changed after freezing; the hashes above let anyone check that the released files are byte-identical to what we post today.

How to verify. When the paper is submitted, the code will be public with these three files byte-identical (their comments include some non-English text, which we left in place to keep the hashes valid). Run sha256sum on them and compare with the list above, then run "python3 confirm_p1p5.py selftest --coder DIR" (DIR = the folder containing trace_events.py), which should print "SELFTEST PASS analysis 1.1".
